text:
As I was intent only on my chimera,

I did not notice what was around me; one day

fertile spring surprised me,

smiling over all the broad field.


Green leaves were budding

from the swollen buds of the branches,

and yellow, white, red flowers

cheered the blotch of the landscape.


And it was a rain of golden arrows,

the sun over the youthful fronds;

in the broad river's sonorous current

the graceful poplars gazed at themselves.


After so much road, it is the first

time I have watched spring break forth,

I said, and afterward, declaimingly:


"How late now for my happiness!"

And then, as I walked, like one who feels

wings of another illusion: "And still

I shall reach my youth one day!"

translation.title: Perhaps
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps Machado's turn from belated spring recognition to the renewed illusion of youth.
